data.text:
It loves not realities and creators, but names and customs.
So do you multiply your presence, or spread yourself throughout your estate.
Action is with the scholar subordinate, but it is essential.
Coleridge, the poet, wrote of Chaucer: "I take unceasing delight in Chaucer; his manly cheerfulness is especially delicious to me in my old age.
There is somewhat not philosophical in heroism; there is somewhat not holy in it; it seems not to know that other souls are of one texture with it; it has pride; it is the extreme of individual nature.

Every soul is by this intrinsic necessity quitting its whole system of things, its friends, and home, and laws, and faith, as the shellfish crawls out of its beautiful but stony case, because it no longer admits of its growth, and slowly forms a new house.
Men seek to be great; they would have offices, wealth, power, and fame.
At home I dream that at Naples, at Rome, I can be intoxicated with beauty, and lose my sadness.
In the case of Shakspeare there is much more.
If our young men miscarry in their first enterprises, they lose all heart.

If they were at a perfect understanding in any part, no words would be necessary thereon.
Of Carthage, a famous ancient city, and state of northern Africa.
For the rest, I like to see that we cannot be bought and sold.
